title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: device health reporting dashboard (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing's portal paths, query, licensing and reporting windows agree with Microsoft documentation. The roadmap details match the records, and targeted searches found no published dashboard-specific default, automation interface or separate charge.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview has a device health reporting dashboard for Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: The device health reporting dashboard in Microsoft Purview gives compliance and security administrators a centralized view of device readiness for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (Endpoint DLP).

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-06-09T20:46:16.
Endpoint DLP extends Purview DLP protection to Windows and macOS devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity detection and protection capabilities of DLP to sensitive items that are physically stored on Windows 10, Windows 11, and macOS (Catalina 10.15 and higher) devices.

claims.claim: The dashboard identifies devices that might not receive or enforce Endpoint DLP policies because of configuration, connectivity or version issues.
claims.quote: The dashboard helps you find devices that might not be ready to receive or enforce Endpoint DLP policies because of configuration, connectivity, or version issues.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes viewing device health across devices and quickly identifying devices that are not ready for policy updates.
claims.quote: This dashboard will allow admins to view the device health across all their devices to ensure the system is healthy and ready to receive policy updates and quickly identify devices that are not ready.

claims.claim: The dashboard gathers onboarding, policy update readiness, recent activity and feature readiness into four sections.
claims.quote: Device onboarding; Device readiness to receive policy updates; Last time devices were seen online; Device readiness for feature

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The sources do not announce changes to existing Endpoint DLP behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "device health reporting dashboard" "automatically" "enable". Read the dashboard page and roadmap record: they describe monitoring and investigation, not a change to Endpoint DLP enforcement.

claims.claim: Access requires Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: To access the device health reporting dashboard, you must have one of the following roles: Compliance Administrator; Security Administrator; Global Administrator

claims.claim: Learn says Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator is sufficient for most organisations.
claims.quote: For most organizations, the Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator role is sufficient.

claims.claim: Per-device attributes include Valid user.
claims.quote: Valid user | This indicates if the currently logged on user has a corresponding Entra ID account and is in scope of a DLP policy that's targeted at Devices.

claims.claim: DlpInfo can contain DlpUpn, identifying the device-associated user.
claims.quote: DlpUpn | string | User principal name (UPN) associated with the device.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The dashboard is a monitoring and investigation view rather than an autonomous enforcement action.
claims.quote: Use the dashboard to monitor device posture at scale, find misconfigured devices, detect devices that might not receive Endpoint DLP policy updates, and validate readiness before deploying new features.

claims.claim: Policy sync status indicates whether a device received the latest policy version.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: Onboarded devices remain in the Devices list for 180 days after going offline.
claims.quote: Onboarded devices will continue to appear for 180 days after the device is offline.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo queries will not work or return results without deployment of the relevant Microsoft Defender service.
claims.quote: If your organization hasn't deployed the service in Microsoft Defender, queries that use the table aren't going to work or return any results.

claims.where: Scope: Out of scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says additional Endpoint DLP features will be added to feature readiness in future releases.
claims.quote: Additional Endpoint DLP features will be added to this section in future releases.

claims.claim: The dashboard is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell cmdlet for the dashboard itself is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "device health reporting dashboard" API PowerShell export. Read dashboard, dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and DeviceInfo pages; results document hunting, policy exports or Defender antivirus reports, not a Purview dashboard interface.

claims.claim: Per-device configuration and policy sync details are reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices > device.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices. ... Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" is a documented advanced hunting query for Endpoint DLP device data.
claims.quote:
Sample query:
DeviceInfo 
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

claims.claim: The query retrieves device attributes using Advanced hunting in the Microsoft Defender portal, rather than changing the dashboard.
claims.quote: To retrieve device attribute data: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal; Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting; Query the DeviceInfo table

claims.claim: DlpInfo supports reporting device configuration status.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices.

claims.claim: DlpInfo supports reporting policy synchronisation status.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices.

claims.claim: DlpInfo supports reporting Endpoint DLP enablement.
claims.quote: IsDlpEnabled | boolean | Indicates whether Endpoint DLP is enabled on the device.

claims.claim: DlpInfo values correspond to device information on the DLP device onboarding page.
claims.quote: These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.claim: Learn does not say the dashboard reads from DeviceInfo.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "device health reporting dashboard" "DlpInfo". Read dashboard, dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and DeviceInfo pages; they link DlpInfo to device onboarding attributes, without identifying it as the dashboard's data source.

claims.claim: Learn's best practices advise regular dashboard reviews and investigating devices that have not reported recently.
claims.quote: Review the dashboard regularly. Frequent checks help you catch device health trends before they become widespread issues. Investigate devices that haven't reported recently.

claims.claim: The feature-readiness section is intended to validate readiness before enabling supported Endpoint DLP features.
claims.quote: Use this section to validate readiness before enabling or deploying Endpoint DLP features across devices.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced hunting enables repeatable analysis of device status beyond the portal view.
claims.quote: The fields in the DlpInfo column correspond directly to the device attributes described earlier. This correspondence enables you to investigate configuration and policy sync issues across multiple devices without relying on point-in-time exports.
